title: Northwestern vs UWMadison: control, tuition, size
summary: Northwestern University (Northwestern) versus University of Wisconsin-Madison (UWMadison). Also searched as UWMadison vs Northwestern. Scorecard table is sourced; prose is checked against those facts. UniRepository is not affiliated with either school.

sections.heading: Cost
paragraphs: Northwestern University vs University of Wisconsin-Madison (Northwestern vs UWMadison) show significant differences in tuition costs. Northwestern University charges $68,322 for both in-state and out-of-state tuition, reflecting its private institution status. In contrast, the University of Wisconsin-Madison has a lower in-state tuition of $11,603, while out-of-state students pay $42,103. Regarding student debt, the median debt for completers at Northwestern is $15,000, whereas at the University of Wisconsin-Madison, it is higher at $20,484. These figures highlight the cost disparities between the two universities, with Northwestern having higher tuition but lower median student debt compared to the University of Wisconsin-Madison.

sections.heading: Learning model and campus
paragraphs: Northwestern University vs University of Wisconsin-Madison (Northwestern vs UWMadison) differ notably in their learning environments and campus settings. Northwestern University, located in Evanston, Illinois, has an undergraduate enrollment of 9,201 students, offering a more intimate campus experience. In contrast, the University of Wisconsin-Madison, situated in Madison, Wisconsin, serves a larger undergraduate population of 36,902 students, reflecting a more extensive campus community. Both institutions provide diverse academic programs, but their campus sizes and student body scales contribute to distinct learning atmospheres.

sections.heading: Accreditation
paragraphs: Northwestern University vs University of Wisconsin-Madison (Northwestern vs UWMadison) are both accredited institutions, ensuring they meet established standards of quality in higher education. sections.heading: Pick Northwestern if
paragraphs: Pick Northwestern if you prefer a private nonprofit institution with a highly selective admission rate of 7.69%. Northwestern University charges $68,322 for tuition regardless of residency, reflecting its private status. The university also boasts a high completion rate of 95.13% within 150% of the expected time, indicating strong student retention and success. These factors make Northwestern an attractive choice for students seeking a rigorous academic environment with a commitment to degree completion.

sections.heading: Pick UWMadison if
paragraphs: Pick UWMadison if you prefer a public university with a more accessible admission rate of 45.2%. The University of Wisconsin-Madison offers in-state tuition of $11,603, which is significantly lower than private institutions, making it a cost-effective option for residents. Additionally, the university has a strong completion rate of 89.55% within 150% of the expected time, reflecting solid student retention and success. These factors make UWMadison a suitable choice for students seeking an affordable public education with a high likelihood of timely degree completion.
